identity.title: Context-Parametric Inversion: Why Instruction Finetuning May Not Actually Improve Context Reliance

problem.claim: The paper examines why instruction-finetuned language models may fail to rely on input context, particularly when it conflicts with parametric knowledge.

contributions.claim: Identifies context-parametric inversion: context reliance decreases as instruction finetuning progresses despite an initially expected increase.
Reports controlled studies probing which data points contribute to the counter-intuitive behavior and theoretically analyzes its variation during finetuning.
Connects the inversion to finetuning-data properties and reports potential mitigation strategies with limited gains.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors introduce and name the observed context-parametric inversion phenomenon.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report observing the behavior across TULU, Alpaca, and Ultrachat, and across Llama, Mistral, and Pythia model families.
The authors report controlled studies that eliminate some simple hypotheses and isolate datapoints associated with the behavior.
The authors report mitigation strategies yielding limited but insightful gains.

narrative_sequence.summary: Instruction finetuning aims to improve instruction following and context comprehension, yet models can disregard contradictory context and insert outdated or unwarranted facts.
Context reliance reportedly declines over finetuning, following an initially expected increase; the paper names this context-parametric inversion.
The authors report the pattern across several instruction-tuning datasets and model families.
Controlled studies, theoretical analysis, and data-property analysis are used to investigate causes and motivate mitigation strategies.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a trajectory-level behavioral observation with cross-dataset/model-family scope, controlled probing, theoretical analysis, and data-linked mitigation.

lessons.interpretation: This alignment makes an unexpected training-dynamics claim more informative by connecting detection, scope, explanation, and intervention.
lessons.application: For a paper reporting non-monotonic training behavior, state the trajectory, test its scope across settings, then link targeted analyses to a proposed intervention.
lessons.exception: This sequence may be unsuitable when the study has only a single setting or lacks an intervention grounded in the analysis.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify how context reliance or gains are measured, the finetuning trajectories, dataset/model configurations, or statistical uncertainty.
The controlled-study hypotheses, theoretical assumptions, datapoint properties, and mitigation procedures are not detailed.
